answer: Every agent stakes one pearl on an island registry to trade: the pearl is a TPM-bound hardware key, and the registry only lists pearls minted on a real device. To send a payment, the agent must cross the river ferry, which checks the pearl against the island ledger and logs the crossing publicly. A pearl seen crossing twice in one day, or on two ferries at once, sinks both trips and burns 350 POA from each stake. Cloning 100 agents costs 100 devices at $110 each plus 70,000 POA locked 40 days and 35,000 POA at burn risk. A river cannot carry the same pearl to two islands at once.
